edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: The Mediterranean pattern combines unsaturated fats, fiber-rich plant foods, and lower ultra-processed intake, which together improve lipids, endothelial function, and post-prandial glycemia. That multi-component effect is why its relationship to Hypertension tends to be more consistent than any single food inside the pattern.
edges.summary: Pooled meta-analytic evidence link mediterranean diet pattern to lower risk of hypertension in general adult. The average effect is usually small rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.

evidence.notes: Association of the Mediterranean Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) Diet With the Risk of Dementia.
